mcqs.question: A metal spring is stretched by a force of 10 N and then released. Which of the following best describes the restoring force acting on the spring at the instant it is released?

options.A: A force equal to 10 N acting opposite to the direction of stretch
options.C: A force equal to 5 N in the same direction as the stretch
options.D: A force that continues to increase with time

mcqs.answer: A force equal to 10 N acting opposite to the direction of stretch
mcqs.explanation: When the spring is released, it exerts a force opposite to the direction of the applied stretch. By Hooke's law the magnitude of this restoring force equals the applied force (10 N) but acts in the opposite direction, trying to bring the spring back to its equilibrium length. Options B, C and D contradict the definition of a restoring force.

mcqs.question: When a rubber band is pulled and then allowed to return to its original length, the property that allows it to regain its shape is called:
mcqs.explanation: Elasticity is the ability of a material to resume its original shape after the deforming force is removed. The rubber band stretches (deforms) and then returns, illustrating elasticity. Plasticity, ductility and brittleness describe other behaviours.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines plasticity?

options.A: The ability of a material to return to its original shape after the removal of load
options.B: The tendency of a material to fracture under small stress
options.C: The permanent deformation of a material after the applied stress exceeds its elastic limit
options.D: The capacity of a material to conduct electricity

mcqs.answer: The permanent deformation of a material after the applied stress exceeds its elastic limit
mcqs.explanation: Plasticity refers to permanent (irreversible) deformation once the stress goes beyond the elastic limit. Option A describes elasticity, B describes brittleness, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: If a steel rod is subjected to a tensile force that is less than its proportional limit, which of the following statements is true about its deformation?

options.A: The rod will undergo permanent deformation
options.B: The rod will return to its original length after the force is removed

mcqs.answer: The rod will return to its original length after the force is removed
mcqs.explanation: Below the proportional (elastic) limit, deformation is elastic, meaning the material returns to its original dimensions once the load is removed. Hence B is correct; A, C and D describe plastic or failure behaviour which do not occur under these conditions.

mcqs.question: Consider two materials, Material X and Material Y, both subjected to increasing tensile stress. Material X returns to its original shape after the stress is removed up to a stress of 200 MPa, but deforms permanently beyond that. Material Y shows permanent deformation even at stresses as low as 50 MPa. Which material exhibits primarily elastic behaviour and which exhibits primarily plastic behaviour?

options.A: X is elastic, Y is plastic
options.B: X is plastic, Y is elastic

mcqs.answer: X is elastic, Y is plastic
mcqs.explanation: Material X behaves elastically up to a relatively high stress (200 MPa) and only becomes plastic beyond that, indicating dominant elastic behaviour. Material Y deforms plastically at low stresses (50 MPa), showing it is primarily plastic. Therefore option A correctly matches the behaviours.

mcqs.question: In a simple harmonic oscillator consisting of a mass attached to a spring, the restoring force is directly proportional to the displacement from equilibrium. Which of the following expressions correctly represents this restoring force?
mcqs.explanation: Hooke's law states that the restoring force exerted by a spring is F = -kx, where k is the spring constant and x is the displacement from equilibrium; the negative sign indicates the force acts opposite to the displacement. Options B, C, and D do not represent a linear restoring force and are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: Elasticity is best described as:

options.A: The ability of a material to undergo permanent deformation
options.B: The ability of a material to return to its original shape after removal of deforming forces
options.C: The resistance of a material to any deformation
options.D: The tendency of a material to break under stress

mcqs.answer: The ability of a material to return to its original shape after removal of deforming forces
mcqs.explanation: Elasticity specifically refers to the reversible deformation—returning to the original shape—once the applied force is removed. Option A describes plasticity, C is vague, and D describes brittleness.

mcqs.question: Plasticity refers to:

options.A: The ability of a material to return to its original shape
options.B: The ability of a material to undergo permanent deformation without breaking
options.C: The ability of a material to conduct heat
options.D: The ability of a material to resist corrosion

mcqs.answer: The ability of a material to undergo permanent deformation without breaking
mcqs.explanation: Plasticity is the property that allows a material to deform permanently (remain deformed) when the applied stress exceeds its elastic limit, without fracturing. Option A is elasticity, while C and D are unrelated properties.
